title: King and pawn: the opposition
summary: In pawn endings the kings fight; the side that takes the opposition wins the race.
body:
With king and pawn against king, the **kings decide** the result.

- **Opposition:** kings face each other with one square between them. The side *not* to move has the opposition and wins the standoff.
- **Attacker:** put your king **in front of** your pawn, not behind it. A king on the 6th rank in front of its pawn always wins (except rook pawns).
- **Defender:** stand in front of the pawn and take the opposition when the enemy king approaches.

examples.prompt: White to move and win. Where does your king belong?
examples.explain: Ke3! takes the opposition (kings on e3 and e5, Black to move). Black must give way and your king marches in front of the pawn. Every other move draws.
Go forward with the king, not the pawn: Kd6 (or Ke6/Kf6) reaches the sixth rank in front of the pawn, which always wins.
Ke5! takes the opposition. Any other king move lets White's king get in front of the pawn and win.
